accordion.title: Accordion
accordion.lead:
A stack of native `<details>` disclosures, one per payload entry. Because the disclosure is the
browser's own element, open/close, keyboard support and find-in-page keep working without script.

form.lead:
Form renders a schema of groups and fields into a real `form`, and owns the parts a plain form does
not: multi-step gating, cascading (conditional) fields, live calculation, validation messages, and
the submit payload.

Fields themselves are components. The form builds the layout and calls the field adapters, so a
field's look still belongs to `@aio-ui/input`; the form only positions it.

<!-- part: id=payload -->

Payload.text:
An array of groups, each with an optional `group` array of field nodes (or nested rows). The shape of
a field node is the input package's contract, not this one.

<!-- part: id=group-row-keys -->

### Group and row keys

A field node **is** the input schema — `{ content, config }` — so its keys (`content.type`,
`content.label`, `config.required`, `config.wide`, `config.csv`, …) belong to `@aio-ui/input`;
this package adds only the cascade rule `condition` beside the two blocks. It reads `config.wide`
whenever it lays a container out: a **row** always grids, a **group** only when it declares
`column`. `wide` is a **percentage of the row** and the only way to size a field — `20`, `"40%"`,
`0.5` (fraction), `"auto"` / `100` (the whole row). **Absent `wide` means an equal share of the
line**: three children under `column: 3` are a third each (34/33/33), and a fourth — or any child
that no longer fits — starts the next line and takes it whole. Declare `wide` only when a line
should be uneven; `column` is also the cap, so the fourth child of a `column: 3` row wraps.

Supported syntax.text:
Four behaviour engines, one flag each. A flag only opens the door: the engine itself is a module,
and when it is absent the form degrades to a no-op instead of throwing. The form never imports an
engine or a sibling package — `FORM_ADAPTER_MANIFEST` is the default stack, and the host composes
the rest.

<!-- part: id=register -->

### Registering the form

<!-- part: id=direct -->

### Without a shell (direct `new FormBuilder`)

No registry, no `AioApp`: build the form yourself and hand it the modules it may use. Three
shapes, and only one of them is a loader input. **The builder ships no stack of its own** since
`0.2.2`: the adapters live behind `@aio-ui/form`, so importing `@aio-ui/form` does not
compile a single engine.

**One import is the whole form.** `FORM_ADAPTER_DEFINITIONS` is nine entries: the four engines,
`input`, and the four field modules (`dropdown`, `file`, `controls`, `popover`, imported from their
`@aio-ui/input/<subpath>` entries). `prepare()` routes them by id — ids in `INPUT_MODULE_IDS` become the
field preset, everything else is loaded as a form feature — which is the same rule
`provideModules()` uses for a manifest. So a hand-wired form gets a real dropdown, a real
uploader and a real action set from one line. `bundle-probe` proves all nine are in that graph
and none of them in the root's.

Two rules, both enforced now:

- **A ref is not a definition.** `{ id, path, export }` is data for `ComponentRegistry` or
  `resolveModuleDefinitions()`; a loader takes `{ id, load }`. Registering a ref used to be
  accepted silently and fail later as `No module rendered the field` — it now throws
  `RegistryError` with code `INVALID_DEFINITION` and names both shapes.
- **A missing capability speaks.** Without a module the field keeps working, in a plainer
  shape: a `dropdown` becomes a native `<select>` over the same options, an uploader becomes a
  plain file input, a popover is not attached. None of that is silent any more — each one
  warns once per builder and emits `moduleMissing`, and the two cases a warning cannot cover
  **throw** with the fix in the message: a declared `config.actions` with no `controls` module
  (buttons would never exist), and a `config.files` policy with no `file` module (the policy
  would receive no files and the bytes would be dropped).

`@aio-ui/form` lists `@aio-ui/input` under **`dependencies`**, not peers: installing the form
tarball brings its field layer with it, so the second URL is not something a consumer has to
know about.

A builder with **no** `modules` still renders — that is the floor: `inputFormAdapter` (every
field) plus `dropdownInputModule` (the field module a first schema always reaches for). Passing
`modules` or `inputModules` replaces the set, and a declared module with the same id wins. Only an
**explicitly empty** loader throws on the first `create()`, naming the import that fixes it: a
form told to run on nothing cannot render one field, and failing per field halfway through a
schema would only hide that.

`resolveModuleDefinitions()` is async and must be awaited **before** `create()`: a builder's render
is synchronous and never owns module I/O.

<!-- part: id=validation -->

### Validation

The rules are the fields' own DOM attributes (`required`, `pattern`, `min`, `max`, `minlength`,
`maxlength`). You declare them in the field's `config` bag; the input adapter puts them on the
control. The engine reads the rendered attributes at submit or at `next`, so a message never
appears while the user is still typing.

<!-- part: id=cascade -->

### Cascade

`condition` on a field is the whole declaration: while the condition is false the field is not in
the DOM. `cascadeMode` decides whether it is built and hidden (`"hidden"`) or planted as a
`<template>` (`"template"`, the default). Use `"hidden"` when another engine needs a live element
to inject into — a chained address picker, for example.

<!-- part: id=calculation -->

### Calculation

`calculation: true` turns the engine on; a field opts in with `config.calculator`. The engine walks
the schema, runs each formula against the current values and writes the total into `outputId`.

<!-- part: id=multistep -->

### Multistep

`multistep: true` turns each group into a step. `prepare()` plants a `<template data-step>` in place
of every step and the fieldset is built when that step is opened, so a heavy step costs nothing
until it is reached. Validation is scanned per step: a step that has not been opened cannot block
the one the user is on.

<!-- part: id=nodes role=contract -->

<!-- part: id=tokens role=contract -->

### Structure

One `fieldset` per group; a row is a `div.row` and a field is the `@aio-ui/input` markup. The id
is derived from config, never from the payload.

Free-typed addresses turn a database into unstructured data: spelling drifts, abbreviations differ,
postal codes go missing and nothing can be validated or aggregated. A cascade over the official

input.title: Input
input.lead:
Input renders **one form field** — label, control, info line — and the shell around it
(switch, file chip, action buttons, popover). A field is a field with or without a form
around it, so nothing in this package is scoped under `.form`; rows, fieldsets and
multistep layout belong to `@aio-ui/form`.

Sub-modules extend the field without changing the builder: `dropdown` (select/search),
`picker` (a grid of icons, swatches or images), `file-uploader`, `controls` (action buttons)
and `popover`. Each one is an `iInputAdapter` that the builder resolves once per `prepare()`
and disposes on teardown.

<!-- part: id=payload -->

**The builder is an element factory.** It assembles the markup below, and `Input.css` only targets
those classes and tokens. The CSS therefore behaves like a plain CSS library: the same nesting and
class names written by hand are styled identically. Customise it by overriding a selector, or
retheme it without touching markup by redeclaring a `--app-*` token on an ancestor (or one
`--input-*` token for this component only). Nothing here is scoped under `.form`.

<!-- install:begin -->

Payload.text:
A field is two blocks: **`content`** is what the field _is_, **`config`** is how it
_behaves_. `InputSchema<T>` narrows both to the chosen `content.type`, so a `file` field
never sees a picker's view word and a text field never sees `options`.

`content` — identity (`type`, `id`, `name`), readable text (`label`, `placeholder`, `info`),
the value (`value`, `checked`) and the choices (`options`, on a chooser only).

`config` — constraints (`required`, `min`/`max`/`step`, `minlength`/`maxlength`, `pattern`,
`accept`, `inputmode`, `rows`/`cols`, `multiple`), state (`disabled`, `readonly`, `editable`,
`loading`, `error`), layout (`position`, `useLabel`, `display`, `wide`, `attributes`,
`view`, `shape`, `column`), callbacks (`onFileSelected`, `calculator`) and module settings
(`actions`, `popover`, `apiUrl`, `debounceDelay`, `onSelect`, `onMultiChange`, `expanded`,
`searchable`, `thumbnail`, `maxUpload`, `maxFileSize`, `groupUnallowed`, `csv`).

`error` is the host's validation state: `true` marks the field invalid, a string marks it
invalid **and** prints the message as a `@field>error` line just above `info`. `loading` puts
the `loading` class on the control — it replaced the old `className: "loading"` shortcut.

A field has exactly one spelling on each side. `label` is the caption — the old `title`
alias is gone, and choices live in `content.options` only (a `config.options` bag is no
longer read). `@aio-ui/form` sends this same shape: its adapter splits a flat form node into
`content` and `config` before it calls `create()`.

`config.view` is the one visual-variant word, typed per field type: `toggle` (checkbox/
radio), `select`/`datalist` (dropdown), `icon`/`image`/`media`/`swatch` (picker) and
`list`/`thumbnails` (file). It replaced the old `style` (dropdown/toggle) and the uploader's
own `view`.

### Width — `wide` is a percentage of the row

`config.wide` is the **only** width knob: `20`, `"40%"`, `0.5` (fraction) or `"auto"` / `100`
(the whole row); absent means the whole row. The old `span` key is **gone** — a column span
cannot express `20 / 40 / 40`, so the form lays a 100-unit grid out from the percentage
(`@aio-ui/form` owns the placement; see its README).

### Action set — `config.actions`

`config.actions` takes names (`"editor"` = edit+save, `"repeater"` = add+delete) or objects
`{ type, label?, icon?, onClick, … }`. Two flags belong to the **`delete`** of a repeater:

The old `minItems` / `atMin` pair is gone: counting rows could not say "keep index 0".

### Choices — one door for every chooser

`options` is content and `multiple` is a constraint, so they sit on opposite sides of the
same field: `content.options` feeds `select`, `dropdown`, `picker` and a `radio`/`checkbox`
group, and `config.multiple` means the same thing in all four:

A `radio`/`checkbox` field **with `options`** renders a group — one control per option, all
on the field's `name`, `radio` exclusive and `checkbox` taking several — and the group's
caption is not a `<label for>`, because there is no single control. Without `options` the
field is the single control it always was.

<!-- part: id=config role=contract -->

Config.text:
`modules: null` is a complete field: a plain labelled control. The four sub-modules are an
enhancement, not a precondition — see below. Pass an already-resolved adapter array when a
parent already loaded the set: the field then never loads or unloads modules the host owns
(that is what `Form` does).

<!-- part: id=modules -->

### Modules — load only what you use

Five sub-modules hang off the field: `dropdown` (a whole builder), `picker` (a grid behind
one control), `file` (the uploader), `controls` (the action set) and `popover`. **None of them
is compiled into the package root** — `scripts/bundle-probe.mjs` proves it against the parsed
module graph. Ask for all five with one import:

A `picker` field is one grid behind one control — icons, swatches or images. The look is
flat on `config`; the choices and the multiplicity stay on the field:

`view` decides what a cell draws: `icon` (a global `i.icon.<name>` class, the option value
by default), `image` / `media` (`src`), `swatch` (`color`). The value reaches the form through
a hidden input named after the field, joined with commas when `multiple` is on.

Each subpath is a builder **and** its module definition — there is no separate `/module` door
since `0.2.4`. Take one without instantiating the other four:

The two shapes, and what each is for:

- `INPUT_MODULE_DEFINITIONS` (`@aio-ui/input`) — what `modules` and `ModuleLoader` take:
  `{ id, load }`.
- `INPUT_MODULE_MANIFEST` (`@aio-ui/input`) — the same list as `{ id, path, export }` refs, for an
  AST whose host lets `ComponentRegistry` (or `resolveModuleDefinitions()`) resolve them. Strings
  only, which is why the root can export it without pulling a single module in.

**A ref is not a definition.** Handing a ref to a loader now throws
`RegistryError` / `INVALID_DEFINITION` at registration instead of failing later as a field with
no control. Order is decorate order (`controls` before `popover`); a trimmed preset that keeps
`popover` but drops `controls` still works, it just anchors to the field wrapper instead.

**What a missing module costs — and says.** A field is never a hole, and a degradation is
never silent. `packages/components/input/Missing.ts` is the single voice:

Every warning is one `console.warn` **and** a `moduleMissing` event through `config.emit`
(`{ builder, capability, module, fix, consequence, severity }`), so an app can surface it in
its own UI instead of reading a console. The throws name the capability, the module id and the
one subpath that fixes it — a declared action set that renders no buttons is a hole, not a
plainer control, so a warning would not be enough. `__tests__/Modules.test.ts` walks every
declared type with `modules: []` and asserts a control still exists; `__tests__/Missing.test.ts`
pins the sentences.

<!-- part: id=nodes role=contract -->

Tokens.text:
### Popup placement

`select::picker(select)`, `.dropdown > .menu` and the picker panel share one surface that is
placed by **CSS Anchor Positioning** and shown by the **Native Popover API** — so they escape
any `overflow: hidden` ancestor and follow the field on scroll and resize without a JS
position calculator. The anchor is the field-scoped name `--field-dropdown-anchor`
(`anchor-scope` on `.field`), never a generated id.

`position-try-fallbacks: --flip-top, flip-block` opens the surface **upward** when there is
no room below; a `@position-try` rule may only carry placing/sizing declarations, so the
mirror is geometric. Anchor positioning and the fallback need Chromium 125+ / Firefox 132+ /
Safari 18+; older engines keep the absolute fallback the surface already declares. The
trigger's own border does not mirror the flip (it is the anchor, not an anchored element, so
it cannot query the chosen fallback); the menu overlaps the trigger by 1px, so the seam
reads as one line in both directions.

Every token is declared **once**, on `:root, [data-theme]`, in `Input.css`. `[data-theme]`
is required: a theme puts `--app-*` on the shell element, and a custom property is
substituted where it is _declared_. Never redeclare these per `.field` — the whole subtree
would inherit the copy and any ancestor override would be shadowed.

Overriding is the third layer: redeclare `--input-*` on any ancestor, leave the package
alone.

**Colour** (derived from `--app-*`)

Dark mode re-derives seven of them in the same file, because the palette inverts the field
(solid border becomes translucent, tinted surface becomes flat) and no single formula
covers both modes.

**File module** (`FileUploader/FileUploader.css`)

**Picker module** (`InputPicker/InputPicker.css`) — declared on `:root, [data-theme]`, every
one derived from the field layer so a theme retunes the picker with the field:

**Metrics and motion** (`Input.css`)

`--input-font-size`, `--input-label-size` (`0.75 × font-size`), `--input-border-radius`,
`--input-line-height`, `--input-icon-size`, `--input-min-height`, `--input-picker-height`
(`3 × line-height`), `--input-dropdown-arrow-content` (SVG data URI),
`--input-dropdown-transition-delay`, `--input-popup-duration`, `--input-popup-easing`,
`--input-popup-distance`.

The loading spinner is **not** an input token: it is shared with the form package and lives
in the app layer as `--app-spinner-content`.

Config.text:
### Outline

An outline renders named parts instead of the whole document, in the order you list them.
The parts are answered from the same parse, so nothing is rebuilt as text and parsed twice.

Trails match on text **and** length: `Config` never resolves to `Config > Notes`.

A selection carries its subsections with it, so `#config` renders the `###` blocks written
under `## Config` — a document never needs one pointer per heading level.

### Markers

A marker is a line no Markdown renderer shows, read as a pointer and attached to the heading
under it. That keeps a page from hard-coding heading text: rename the heading, keep the anchor.

`id` overrides the slug the heading text would produce; `role` is a word the parser hands back
and never interprets; any other `key=value` pair is kept. A comment that does not match the
keyword is dropped rather than printed, because it is invisible in every other renderer too.
Only a comment alone on its line counts — a trailing comment stays part of the paragraph, and
anything inside a fence stays source.

examples.code:

Multi-level.text:
One entry that carries a nested list is a **branch**. The list is the same element at every depth —
`ul.menus` — and the recursion is the builder's: `paintList()` renders `@menu>menus`, and each of
those items runs `paintItem()` again, so depth is bounded only by the data.

Contract the sheet relies on:

- `nav[data-multilevel="<activation>"]` — config, stamped once on the bar, only when `activation` is one of the three strings.
- `li.item.submenu` — the branch; `open` / `closed` is the state the builder flips.
- `li.item.submenu.is-active` — a branch that contains the current route.
- The glyph is an icon, not a bespoke caret: a branch is rendered with `icon: "icon arrow right"`
  (overridable per entry) and the sheet turns it a quarter for the closed state. Swap the string
  when the icon set grows an `arrow down`.
- A branch never navigates: its click belongs to the disclosure, and its `href` is not bound. Make the
  group's own page its first child instead.
- `Escape` closes what a click opened.

Below `768px` **every position looks the same** — a `top` bar and a `left` / `right` column both
collapse to a strip:

Above the breakpoint each position keeps the behaviour it asked for: a bar hangs popovers, a column
draws an inset list.

It is a **media query, not a resize observer**: the sheet has nothing to measure — the host decides
how wide the aside is — and every rule is a function of the viewport. If a host needs the collapse
keyed to the _column_ instead, it declares `container-type: inline-size` on the wrapper and copies
these rules into a `@container` block; the sheet cannot do that for it.

### `duration` — lifetime, not pulse

The builder's default is `2000`, not `"auto"`: on a warm cache the sheet settles in a single
microtask, so an `"auto"` placeholder is never painted and the component appears to have no
loading state at all. `"auto"` stays available for a host that measures the sheet itself.

stylesheet promise (`Promise.all`). A skeleton never hides anything itself, and a warm sheet never
builds one. The pulse _speed_ is a different knob: `--skeleton-pulse` in this package's layer.

table.title: Table
table.lead:
Table renders a header, a body and a footer from one data object, and owns the behaviour a static
table does not: pagination, sorting, selection, inline editing, per-cell options and row formulas.

Cells may be plain values or objects shaped `{ text, options }` — `options` is a `TableCellOptions`
(`class`, `color`, `wide`, `textAlign`, `verticalAlign`, `rowSpan`, `colSpan`, `format`, `formula`). The
helper exports (`__normalizeCell`, `__applyCellOptions`, `__applyFormula`, `numberToText`) are the same
functions the builder uses, so a host can reuse them.

**The builder is an element factory.** It assembles the markup below, and `Table.css` only targets
those classes and tokens. The CSS therefore behaves like a plain CSS library: the same nesting and
class names written by hand are styled identically. Customise it by overriding a selector, or
retheme it without touching markup by redeclaring a `--app-*` token on an ancestor (or one
`--table-*` token on the table's parent).
